sentences.text: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act is also known as MGNREGA.
It was enacted in 2005 to enhance livelihood security in rural areas.
The main objective is to provide at least 100 days of unskilled wage employment in a financial year to every rural household.
The scheme aims to improve livelihood security and create durable assets in rural areas.
Benefits include guaranteed wage employment and the creation of public works.
The assistance is provided in the form of wages for unskilled manual work.
Eligibility is limited to adult members of rural households.
Households must apply for a job card to avail of the benefits.
The application process involves submitting a request to the local Gram Panchayat.
The timeline for employment is within 15 days of applying for work.
The implementing authority is the Ministry of Rural Development.
State governments are responsible for implementing the scheme at the local level.
The scheme is funded by the central government and state governments.
It also aims to empower marginalized communities by providing them with work opportunities.
Regular monitoring and evaluation are conducted to ensure effective implementation.
The scheme has provisions for grievance redressal to address issues faced by beneficiaries.
